Async terminal success can expose exact effect OID after UUID/intent reconciliation; failure lacks a documented exact ref-update SHA and remains family-specific UNKNOWN without another binding.
Merge queue and stacked PR verification needs explicit coverage of every relevant merge-group/final-base effect; one terminal OID is not presumed complete.

Dynamic resource-authorization scope freshness is independent of tool-surface freshness; current scope observations are not leases/CAS tokens.
MCP Roots is deprecated/informational in the current specification; only independently proven server implementation enforcement counts as authorization evidence.
Repository role evidence, server-enforced resource scope, exact credential/operation authorization, and post-call success are distinct evidence levels.
